newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. troops to come home in a year.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. troops to come home in a year.

text.p: President Bill Clinton vowed anew on Sunday to bring U.S. troops home from a NATO peace-keeping force in Bosnia in a year's time despite European concern that a pullout could prompt a new cycle of bloodshed.
"Our policy is the mission should be completed by June 1998 and we expect it to be," Clinton said in a news conference concluding the Group of Seven summit here.
America has 8,500 troops in the 31,000-strong NATO force in Bosnia. Europeans fear an American pullout would lead to the collapse of the force.
European leaders at the G7 summit expressed concern to Clinton on Friday night about his plans to withdraw the troops on schedule.

At the news conference, Clinton said he told his summit colleagues that they were spending too much time focusing on June 1998 instead of concentrating on what can be done now to prop up the faltering Bosnian peace process.
He predicted that in the next few months there would be a number of examples showing progress in the peace process.
